content: I wanted to check whether anyone is working on proving Myhill-Nerode in CSLib—the recent contribution of right congruences to Cslib.Computability can be used to do this. If no one else is working on this, I'm happy to contribute.

Hi, thanks for the interest in contributing! CSLib automata are defined separately from Mathlib, but there is already file#Computability/MyhillNerode. But I really don't know this area that well, maybe this looks different given how RightCongruence is formulated. I'll probably defer to @Ching-Tsun Chou on if we'd like a different version of this.

I think the version of Myhill-Nerode theorem in mathlib is not standard and it would be a good addition to cslib if the standard version of the theorem can be added:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myhill%E2%80%93Nerode_theorem
The notion of right congruence and some related results are already in cslib:
https://api.cslib.io/docs/Cslib/Computability/Languages/Congruences/RightCongruence.html
https://api.cslib.io/docs/Cslib/Computability/Automata/DA/Congr.html
https://api.cslib.io/docs/Cslib/Computability/Languages/RegularLanguage.html#Cslib.Language.IsRegular.congr_fin_index
The current version mathlib version is a good starting point. I think it’s from Dexter Kozen’s book. It just needs a few extra steps to deduce the automata states version.

The most general version of the theorem is to take two equivalence relations on a language

  1. ~R is the suffix relation which says that two strings are equiv iff adding each possible identical suffix makes them both accepting or not.
  2. ~L(A) is defined w.r.t a specific automaton A. Two strings are equiv if they both end up at the same state on A from the starting state.

Then you show four things.

  1. \forall A, |states(A)| = |L\~L(A)|. This mathlib doesn’t do yet
  2. forall A, ~L(A) refines ~R : this is what mathlib seems to do already.
  3. You can define an automaton A’, such that L(A’) = ~R. Its states are the elements of the quotient L\~R This mathlib does .
  4. A’ has the smallest cardinality of sets for any A recognising L. Not in mathlib afaict.

I just looked up Kozen’s book. I think its development of the Myhill-Norode theorem is closer to that in Wikipedia. Anyway, it’s a very nice development and some parts of it are already in cslib. It shouldn’t be hard to formalize the rest.
